answer: Proposed: a tundra atlas service tests jetty relay agents in one daily 10-second window. Each key must echo a distinct random 1 GB stream within it. Independent auditors measure full echoes and sign key/day receipts; validators deny pay for missing, late, invalid or reused receipts. Collusion defeats checks; burst rental is allowed, so this proves neither unique owners nor continuous uptime. Link rental/power recur; routers are reusable capital; no stake is locked. Even on shared links, ten parallel keys still need 8 Gbit/s aggregate egress versus 0.8 for one, ignoring overhead.
